text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000120 bills 99215 at elevated rates in every complexity band, including simple acute visits, but the few returned charts support the billed levels, so the evidence is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern leans toward upcoding. The 99215 share runs about two to two-and-a-half times the all-provider share in every complexity band, including patients with zero conditions, so a sicker panel alone does not explain it. The sampled low-complexity 99215s are mostly routine problems such as upper respiratory infection (C0059945, C0060092, C0061024), back pain (C0059908, C0060890), UTI (C0059940, C0060127) and follow-up encounters (C0060059, C0061022), which rarely need high-complexity decision-making. Against that, all 6 documented 99215 claims supported the billed level, with examples showing high MDM and 41-53 minutes (C0059529, C0060164), but 6 charts from 1.3% of claims is too thin to settle the question. The 7 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test on the claim are weak evidence that notes may be templated or inflated to match billing. A reviewer should first pull charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s, especially the zero-condition acute visits, and check them for cloned or templated note text."}
